result.summary: Sets explicit `permissions: contents: read` on the main GitHub Actions CI workflow. This restricts the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` to read-only repository contents access across all CI jobs.
result.problem: CI permissions currently rely on Bitcoin Core's repository-level default setting. In contributor forks where repository defaults might permit broader write permissions, CI runs could execute with unnecessary token privileges.
evidence: Author description: "On this repository the token is already read-only, through the repository's default. The workflow's permissions key then adjusts that default... so the setting now lives in the workflow."
Author references an identical hardening change in libsecp256k1 (bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1964).
result.scope_notes: A 3-line change adding a top-level `permissions` block to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
result.changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the patch; diff is now available confirming the 3-line addition to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
result.card: Sets explicit contents: read permissions on the GitHub Actions CI workflow. This enforces least privilege directly in the workflow definition rather than relying on repository-level default settings, preventing contributor forks from running CI jobs with unintended write privileges. It hardens CI infrastructure with no changes to node software or build outputs.

risk.why: Only alters GitHub Actions CI token permissions; any mistake would at worst break CI workflow execution.
